items.question: How can they come back?
items.text:
The books speak to this, and the way back is not complicated, though it takes honesty.

**Repent and turn.** The weeping prophet's whole message was, "Turn away from your wicked ways. Stop doing evil! Repent and come back to God." That call went out again and again, and it is still the way home [2].

**Reason with God.** God says, "Come now, and let us reason together" (Isaiah 1:18). He is a rational Being who wants to reason with you, so you don't have to put your mind aside to come back — you can bring your whole self to Him and talk it through [3].

**Come back before the point of no return.** There is a line we must not cross, a point of no return. Some say they will backslide and return later, forgetting that there may be no later. So don't delay the turning [3].

**Adapt to your new circumstances instead of using them as an excuse.** Christians who can't adapt to new roles — as wives, husbands, parents, or in a new city or job — often go cold. The counsel is to rise up and adapt quickly rather than turn your back on God because of a new circumstance [5].

**Keep singing the Lord's song wherever you are.** The Lord is your strength and your song and your salvation (Psalm 118:14), and you cannot separate your song from your strength. Even if you are married to an unbeliever, don't give up your walk with the Lord [5].

**Pray, and stay planted.** Jesus told His disciples to pray because they might fall into temptation, and prayer is where the strength to stand comes from [7]. And God expects you to be like a tree planted by the rivers of water — planted in the house of the Lord, with a pastor to relate to, belonging somewhere [7].

If you'd like, we could talk about what to do when someone you love is the one who has drifted.

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapters 1, 7 and 8 of *Backsliding*.

Scriptures referenced: Psalms 118:14; Psalms 137:4; Proverbs 7:10; Isaiah 1:18.

items.question: One of my members says she has no reason to live anymore.
items.text:
That is a heavy thing to carry, and I am glad she has you near her.

Our books have not directly addressed this. They do speak about the shortness of life and the urgency of using the time we have, if that would help.

What they do say is that our time on earth is our one chance, and it is short. One pastor was shown in a vision two dead ministers who came back briefly and found that no one received their messages or sang their songs anymore; they said plainly, "You have the best chance now. This is your time to be fruitful. Our time is past. Our chance is gone. This is your best chance; now!" [2] The same warning is repeated: this is our best chance, and soon we will be out of this world, so we should not serve God in drips and drops but give Him our best while we still can [4]. The book also says that you can best impact your generation whilst you are alive, and that dead people are quickly forgotten [2].

If it would help her, you might sit with her on that: that her life still has a purpose and a work only she can do now.

Please also speak with your shepherd or pastor today. Where a life may be at risk, contact emergency services or a medical professional now.

items.question: What is true forgiveness?
items.text:
True forgiveness is a releasing, not just a feeling. It is choosing to let go of the hurt, bitterness, and wickedness in your heart so that Satan finds a closed door rather than an open one [6]. It means dismissing the painful issues, giving up your claims against the one who hurt you, cancelling what they owe you, and making no more mention of the matter [6]. You stop feeling resentment and anger, and you cancel any punishment you had planned for them [6]. As Ephesians 4:32 says, we are to be kind and tenderhearted, forgiving one another even as God, for Christ's sake, has forgiven us [6].

Forgiveness also means leaving vengeance to God rather than taking it into your own hands. "Vengeance is mine, says the Lord" (Romans 12:19), so you submerge that desire and trust Him to do the avenging [3]. Jesus Himself taught us to pray for God to avenge us, as in Luke 18:6-8, and God has a repayment plan for those who harm you [3]. When you are busy forgiving, you will not have time to avenge yourself [3].

And forgiveness is the doorway to your own healing. You will not get healed if you do not genuinely forgive, and a test of true forgiveness is being able to pray sincerely for the well-being of the one who hurt you [1]. Only then can joy begin to return [1].

items.question: I keep saying hurtful things when I am angry. How do I control my mouth?
items.text:
It's a hard thing to watch your own words wound the people you love, and I'm glad you're bringing it into the light.

- **See the tongue for what it is.** Scripture calls the tongue an unruly evil, full of deadly poison, and says no man can tame it on his own — it takes the Holy Spirit to help a believer control his tongue [3]. So this is not a battle you win by sheer willpower.

- **Recognise that your words carry real power.** Death and life are in the power of the tongue (Proverbs 18:21), and many words spoken are living spirits performing things in the physical realm, so you must watch your mouth and the words you hear [3][7].

- **Refuse corrupt speech.** Let no corrupt communication come out of your mouth, but only what is good for edifying, that it may minister grace to the hearers (Ephesians 4:29) [1]. Profane and vain babblings only increase unto more ungodliness (2 Timothy 2:16), and such talk defiles both the speaker and the hearers [2].

- **Deal with the anger underneath.** Wrath, anger, clamour and evil speaking are signs of lingering unforgiveness, and we are told to put them all away and be kind, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ's sake has forgiven us (Ephesians 4:31-32) [5]. Be angry and sin not; let not the sun go down upon your wrath (Ephesians 4:26) [1].

- **Give no place to the devil.** Neither give place to the devil (Ephesians 4:27) — give no opportunity to your flesh, and flee rather than stand and fight when you are tempted [1][6].

- **Keep your heart free of hurts.** A senior minister once advised, "Always keep your heart pure and free of hurts," and over the years that counsel proved its worth [4].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapter 60 of *Model Marriage*, chapters 1 and 4 of *Poison: Taming The Tongue*, chapter 5 of *Why Few Are Chosen*, chapter 4 of *Forgiveness Made Easy 3rd Edition*, chapter 2 of *Seven Great Principles* and chapter 13 of *Victory Secrets*.

items.question: What should I do when one of them is a leader I trained?
items.text:
That is a particular kind of pain — when the one who leaves is someone you poured yourself into. The books speak to it.

First, know that this is not unusual. One pastor trained a brother, appointed him, and after some years the man dropped a bombshell and left, planting a church nearby and inviting members to follow him [6]. Another trained a 747 pilot into a pastor, and he too broke away to start an independent ministry [4].

When it happens, the counsel is clear. If someone indicates a desire to leave, it is best for them not to stay on but to leave immediately, because their heart has already left the church [5]. One pastor kept a rebellious pastor on after he asked to leave, and the extra months were not worth the trouble they yielded [5]. Jesus Himself told Judas, "That thou doest, do quickly" (John 13:27) [5].

Do not let it spread. If you must resign, resign alone — do not influence others to leave with you [1][2]. The pilot pastor's breakaway released a domino spirit of rebellion; one after another, the pastors who had watched him did exactly the same, and the city was soon dotted with splinter churches and confused members [4].

And guard your own heart. Jesus knew the truth about Peter — that he would deny Him and go back to fishing — yet He did not change His plans for him, and Peter became a great leader of the church [8]. Truth mixed with grace can still produce something beautiful.

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapters 3 and 10 of *Loyalty and Disloyalty*, chapter 4 of *Ministerial Ethics*, chapter 5 of *Those who leave you*, chapter 4 of *Those Who Forget* and chapter 80 of *The Art of Leadership - 3rd Edition*.

Scriptures referenced: Genesis 31:20-22; Numbers 16:3; Numbers 16:8-9; Proverbs 17:13; Ezekiel 34:18; John 13:27; John 13:38; John 21:2-3; 1 Corinthians 5:6.

items.question: Why do some Christians who give tithes prosper while others struggle?
items.book: Why Non Tithing Christians Become Poor And Tithing Christians Become Rich
items.text:
That's a question many faithful givers carry quietly, and the books speak to it directly.

The tithe is meant to be the first fruits of your increase, not the last fruits of your surplus — it changes in its very nature when it is not given first, and that may be why someone gives ten percent and still sees no increase [7]. It must also actually be ten percent; nine percent is not a tithe, and the tithe is ten percent of your increase [7]. And the offering itself must be acceptable — money entering the bowl does not mean it was accepted in Heaven, for offerings are unacceptable because of an unrighteous life, secret idolatry, or not giving in proportion to what was received [7].

Beyond the gift itself, several things can neutralize the blessing. Wrong desires contradict the principles tithing sets in motion — if you desire to kill and fight, God cannot bless you, and you may even find angels opposing you from another angle, for all things work together for your good [1]. Strife with the brethren blocks it too, since the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace by those who make peace [1]. A troubled marriage does the same: strife, bitterness, unforgiveness and hatred neutralize the prayers of the saints, and husbands are told to dwell with their wives in honour so that their prayers are not hindered (1 Peter 3:7) [1]. Hidden sin also cancels blessing, for he who covers his sins shall not prosper, but whoever confesses and forsakes them shall have mercy (Proverbs 28:13) [1].

So the struggle is rarely about the tithe alone — many things work together [1].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapter 22 of *Why Non Tithing Christians Become Poor And Tithing Christians Become Rich*.

Scriptures referenced: Nehemiah 12:43-44; Proverbs 28:13; James 3:18; James 4:2-3; 1 Peter 3:7.

items.question: How can my wife and I build a strong marriage?
items.text:
What a good thing to want to build together. Our books have a good deal to say about this.

- **Make Christ the foundation of your home.** A house built on the rock of hearing and doing Christ's words cannot be shaken when the floods come, as Luke 6:47–48 says, and when God is the focus of both of you, your closeness to Him draws you closer to each other [2].

- **Apply biblical principles and build your marriage around the church.** The Word of God is your manual for marriage, and the man who delights in God's law is like a tree planted by rivers of water, bearing fruit in season, as Psalm 1:1–6 describes [2].

- **Develop family worship.** Hold regular devotions together, or at least each of you regularly and together once in a while with the children; attend church services and sit together, and train your children in the importance of Sundays [2].

- **Think as a Christian spouse, not as one.** Do nothing out of selfish ambition, but in humility consider the other better than yourself, as Philippians 2:3 says; reconcile the plans you each held before marriage, be willing to give up preferences for the sake of the home, and be ready to compromise [2][5].

- **Speak to each other, and speak life.** Speaking the truth in love makes you grow up in Christ, as Ephesians 4:15 says; speaking brings relief and healing, and death and life are in the power of the tongue, as Proverbs 18:21 says, so express your love verbally [4].

- **Guard your friendships and nurture trust.** Have mutual friends as much as possible, and discontinue friendships that don't sit well with your spouse; do everything to make each other feel secure [3].

- **Deal with fear and insecurity through closeness.** Suspicion shows an absence of real love, for perfect love casts out all fear, as 1 John 4:18 says; so forge a closer friendship with each other and vent your fears in the right way and atmosphere [3].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapters 7, 9 and 60 of *Model Marriage*.

items.question: There is a woman in our church who manipulates and controls people. How do I deal with her?
items.book: Jezebel, A Woman Out Of Order
items.text:
This is a heavy thing to carry, and I'm glad you're asking rather than looking away.

The first step is to identify her clearly, because a Jezebel can be defeated if she can be identified [7]. She may look spiritual — even a prophetess or a teacher of the Word — and that disguise is precisely what disarms people and makes them afraid to fight her [6]. Her aim is to isolate and control, as happened when a woman gained such influence over Evan Roberts that she isolated him from his friends, wrote letters in his name, and convinced him to withdraw from ministry altogether; he eventually broke free but never recovered what was destroyed [2].

You cannot deal with this alone. It takes the collective rebuke of church leadership — one person crying foul will not correct or control a Jezebel [3]. The mistake at Thyatira was that she was *allowed* to operate freely, and God held the church accountable for that [7]. So do not let fear of controversy or the wish to keep good relations with everyone keep you silent; if she goes uncorrected, you may lose everything [7][8].

Practically, that means confronting her openly rather than from the shadows, as David put Michal in her place when she came at him with unruly speech [4]. And guard your own soul: insist on being led by the Holy Spirit, not by any man or woman [2].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapters 4, 10, 17 and 21 of *Jezebel, A Woman Out Of Order*, chapter 17 of *What it means to be as Wise as a Serpent* and chapter 15 of *Can’t You Do
Just a Little Bit More?*.

Scriptures referenced: Revelation 2:20.

items.question: What does Loyalty and Disloyalty say about the stages of disloyalty?
items.text:
Disloyalty doesn't happen overnight — it's a process, and most people don't even notice it happening in themselves or in those around them [1]. Here are the stages the book lays out.

- **An independent spirit.** It begins subtly, when someone in a group or ministry becomes autonomous within it — the rules no longer control him, and he obeys only the instructions he thinks are important [1].
- **Offence.** The second stage is offence; Jesus said many would be offended and then betray and hate one another (Matthew 24:10), and the spirit of offence opens the door to treachery [3].
- **Passivity.** After being hurt, a person becomes passive — uninvolved, unconcerned, keeping to himself. Absalom said nothing for two whole years after his sister was disgraced, and that silence was passivity [3][6].
- **The critical stage.** The passive person moves on to noticing and magnifying faults — in the preaching, the order of service, the building. Miriam, who had followed Moses out of Egypt, began to see and speak about his faults [6][5].
- **The political stage.** He then draws others into his ideas, gathering a following and speaking on behalf of "many people" who are unhappy [5][7].
- **Deception.** Those who rebel are grossly deceived; if they were not, they would not do what they do, and most who rebel end in destruction [7].
- **Open rebellion and execution.** Finally comes open fighting against authority, as Lucifer, Absalom and Judas did — and the end of all rebels is the same, for rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft (1 Samuel 15:23) [4].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapter 2 of *Loyalty and Disloyalty*.

items.question: People are spreading lies about me in the church. How should I respond?
items.text:
I'm sorry — that is a heavy thing to carry, and it's painful when it comes from within your own church family.

Our books have not directly addressed this. They do speak about how to handle slander and the fear it spreads, if that would help.

What they do say is this: slanderers spread fear through their stories, and fear is not from God — He gives power, love and a sound mind, as 2 Timothy 1:7 says [1]. So resist the panic that the rumours are trying to plant in you. David's response in Psalm 31 was to trust God and say, "Thou art my God" [1]. You are not required to run the campaign against your accusers; God will deal with those who burn others with the very fuel they planned to use [1].

One caution the books give: don't become a slanderer yourself in return. A slanderer reveals secrets and goes up and down spreading stories, and God calls that evil [6]. Even when you have been wronged, the counsel is to lay hands on your tongue and make sure there is no poison in it [3].

If you'd like, we could look together at what the books say about handling offence and about those who sow discord among brethren.
items.label: answerable

items.question: What does it mean to be a shepherd over a small group of people?
items.book: What It Means to Become a Shepherd
items.text:
Being a shepherd over a small group means you are a caring, loving guide to those sheep — someone God has called to look after them [3]. It is not a title but a job with a shape to it.

- **You give them time.** A shepherd is a specific kind of worker who has time to care, time to love, time to feed and time to gather the sheep [1]. Shepherds belong out among the sheep, not behind a desk [8].

- **You notice their problems.** A good shepherd sees the wolf coming (John 10:12); he knows when his people are doing exams, or facing marital trouble [7].

- **You keep the family together.** The pastoral gift holds people together through the years — old with young, married with unmarried, even enemies under one roof [7].

- **You share the burden.** The burden of leading and accounting for souls cannot be borne by one person; shepherds share the praying, visiting, counselling and interacting with the sheep [8].

It is an honour to be chosen for this, and to have compassion on people [2].

items.question: What do the books teach about IVF for couples who cannot have children?
items.text:
Our books have not directly addressed this. They do speak about family planning and the gift of children, if that would help.

What they do say is that family planning exists so a couple can prevent unwanted pregnancies and space the intervals between their children, and one reason given is that a newly married couple needs time to adjust to each other and learn to communicate and share before the responsibilities of a young family come upon them [7]. They also note that fear of pregnancy can inhibit a couple's enjoyment of the sex relationship [7].

On the question of children themselves, the books speak of fruitfulness in terms of winning souls and making disciples, urging believers to stay active in witnessing, teaching and helping rather than remaining passive, since passive Christians bear no fruit [1][2]. They also encourage stability, describing a tree that is often transplanted as never reaching its full, fruit-bearing potential, and pointing to Psalm 92:13–14, that those planted in the house of the LORD shall still bring forth fruit in old age [2].

If it would help, I can talk with you about what the books say on family planning methods, or about bearing fruit in your walk with God.

items.question: How can I pray more effectively?
items.text:
Prayer that works is worth learning, and our books give clear counsel on it.

- **Pray the prayers of the Bible.** Let your prayers be guided by God's Word, praying the very prayers recorded in Scripture — Ephesians 1:17-19 is one of the most powerful a minister can pray, and Ephesians 3:15-19 prays to be grounded in love, which matters greatly for a pastor [1]. The Ephesians prayer topics walk through thanksgiving, wisdom and revelation, enlightened understanding, knowing your calling, the riches of your inheritance, and the power of God [4].

- **Pray fervently.** Fervent prayer is passionate, ardent, burning and eager — if someone watched you pray, one of those words should describe it, and doodling and dawdling prayers are not fervent [1].

- **Pray in tongues.** Spend hours praying in tongues; Paul boasted, "I thank God that I speak in tongues more than you all" (1 Corinthians 14:18), and this gift lets you speak to God supernaturally [1].

- **Talk with the Holy Spirit.** Prayer is two-way; learn to speak to Him and hear His voice, for as John 14:26 says, the Comforter will teach you all things [1].

- **Pray long, and at set times.** Jesus rose a great while before day to pray (Mark 1:35) and continued all night (Luke 6:12), and Paul prayed night and day (1 Thessalonians 3:10) [1]. Develop the habit of praying morning, afternoon, evening and all-the-time, for "pray without ceasing" (1 Thessalonians 5:17) [3][5].

- **Watch and pray.** Watching — staying awake at night to pray — is mentioned more in the Bible than fasting and praying, and gaining control of your sleep makes you a mighty prayer warrior [7].

- **Repeat the will of God.** Jesus prayed the same words three times about God's will; that was not vain repetition (Matthew 6:7) but meaningful, effective prayer, and it is worth hours [8].

items.question: How can a young person stay away from sexual sin?
items.text:
You're asking a question the books take seriously, and they have real counsel for it.

- **Respect your desires rather than denying them.** Your sexuality is something to be respected, and a proper respect for youthful lusts, rather than a denial of them, will save you from them [4]. Young people sense strong sexual urges that constantly remind them of their lack of holiness, and that feeling can strip away confidence in the things of God [5].

- **Make purity one of your clearest and most energetic goals.** The will of God is your sanctification, that you abstain from sexual immorality, as 1 Thessalonians 4:3-4 says, so stay away from anyone who would want such a relationship with you [3].

- **Find your own way of keeping yourself from fornication.** Everyone has a different way; it may be God's will for you to avoid certain books or films, to marry young, to travel with your wife, or to keep certain friends and working arrangements [3].

- **Avoid untimely relationships.** Very young people should not enter into courtship, for there is a season for everything, as Ecclesiastes 3:1 says [6]. Only enter relationships that lead to marriage, since the only intimate relationship God approves of is marriage [6].

- **Turn from riotous living.** Fooling around with the opposite sex is riotous living, and it is what destroyed the young man in the story of the prodigal son [7]. A young man who develops a taste for a different girl every other day will find it hard to live happily with one woman [7].

- **Be visible, not hidden.** Do not sit at the back or hide in the crowd; make sure your pastor knows your name and sit in the front, because those who sit far away are often practicing some kind of evil [7].

- **Know that holiness is possible for you.** Young people can be empowered by the Spirit of holiness, and age has nothing to do with holiness [8]. Jesus is the best example of a young person who lived a clean life, and there are many young people who have kept the commandments from their youth upward [8].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapter 5 of *The Art of Hearing*, chapters 10, 13 and 24 of *Ready@20*, chapter 35 of *The Art of Shepherding* and chapter 4 of *Spiritual Dangers*.

Scriptures referenced: Genesis 3:16; Psalms 119:9; Ecclesiastes 3:1; Jeremiah 2:5; Matthew 19:16-20; Luke 15:13; Luke 15:15; Luke 15:30; John 8:46; Romans 1:4 and 5 more.

items.question: How can I tell when someone in my team is becoming disloyal?
items.text:
It's wise to want to see this early, because disloyalty doesn't happen overnight — it's a process, and most people don't even notice it in themselves [1]. Here are the signs the books point to:

- **An independent spirit.** Watch for someone who becomes autonomous within the team, no longer governed by its rules, doing what he wants despite contrary instructions — like a person who decides on his own day to fast when the whole group was told to fast on Friday [1].

- **Absence in times of pressure.** Notice who disappears when the church is going through hard times; it's in the heat of events that true character shows [2]. One leader tells of urgently calling church workers to stand with him before government officials during a crisis, and they simply didn't turn up — he felt deeply let down in a time of war [2].

- **Inflexibility.** An inflexible person is stubborn and defiant, unwilling to go beyond what's stipulated, always pointing out that work ends at 5 p.m., and refusing correction when confronted — as Saul argued with Samuel even when the evidence of his disobedience was obvious [3].

- **Silence and quiet satisfaction when things go wrong.** A disloyal assistant has no comment, good or bad, on your new ideas, and is quick to say "I knew this wouldn't work" when something fails [4].

- **Wanting your place.** He thinks he'd be a better head if given the chance, and resents the differences that make him subordinate [4].

- **Criticism and murmuring.** Where members constantly criticise, accuse, murmur and find fault with their leader, there is demonic activity at work — Jesus said of His twelve, "one of you is a devil" (John 6:70) [7].

And remember, loyalty today does not mean loyalty tomorrow [8].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapters 2, 5 and 8 of *Loyalty and Disloyalty*, chapters 4 and 7 of *Those Who Are Ignorant* and chapter 5 of *Know Your Invisible Enemies*.

Scriptures referenced: 1 Kings 1:5-7; John 2:24-25; John 6:70; John 7:3; John 7:5.

items.question: How should a Christian live simply and avoid wasting money?
items.text:
Wanting to live simply and stop wasting money is a good and godly desire, and our books have a great deal to say about it.

- **See waste as a real danger, not a small thing.** If you waste what God has put into your hand you will lose your valued and privileged position, and God will one day ask you to account for what was in your control [1]. Wasters tend to become poor, while those who halt the wastage tend to become rich [1].

- **Cut out waste deliberately.** Most poor nations waste half their resources, which is exactly why they stay poor; they simply have not learned to prevent wastage [6]. Cut your coat according to your size and avoid grandiose, expensive things others are doing [6].

- **Dislike loans and gifts.** Every admirer of gifts and loans is likely to fail in leadership, and many people do not pay back what they borrow [6].

- **Learn to do things with your own hands.** Some people love to sit aloof in an armchair and never roll up their sleeves to work, imagining they are executives when they are not at that level [6].

- **Choose your friends carefully.** The prodigal son did not waste his money alone — there were harlots helping him do it, and bad company will cause you to waste your life away [3]. Evil company corrupts good habits, as 1 Corinthians 15:33 says [3].

- **Beware of get-rich-quick schemes.** Wise businessmen are wary of them, and one such bank collapsed and many people lost their money [4]. There are no short cuts in Christianity [4].

- **Kill wrong desires while they are small.** A strong overpowering desire for material things is what God calls lust, and it destroys [5].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapter 14 of *He That Hath, To Him Shall Be Given: And He That Hath Not, From Him Shall Be Taken Even That Which He Hath*, chapter 10 of *Opportunities*, chapters 3 and 4 of *How you can become a strong Christian* and chapter 2 of *What it means to be as Wise as a Serpent*.

Scriptures referenced: 1 Samuel 30:3-6; Psalms 27:4; Mark 4:19; Luke 15:12-14; Luke 15:25; Luke 16:1-2; 1 Corinthians 15:33.

items.question: What is the secret to answered prayer?
items.text:
The books speak of this often, and they hold out real hope: God's Word guarantees us results every time we pray, and Jesus did not say we might possibly get an answer — He said we would [4][6]. Here are the keys they give.

- **Learn to pray for yourself.** God wants you to be able to come to your heavenly Father directly, not to depend only on your pastor or on prayer warriors; their support is a bonus, not your foundation [5].

- **Let God's Word abide in you.** God does nothing outside His Word, and His Word directs you in prayer; He does not answer foolish prayers or act against His Word, so stay in the Word [1][2].

- **Obey His commandments.** Scripture says we receive what we ask because we keep His commandments and do what pleases Him (1 John 3:22); obedience opens the door, and the fervent prayer of a righteous man avails much (James 5:16) [1][2].

- **Bear fruit.** God has linked answered prayer to fruit-bearing: He chose and ordained us to go and bring forth fruit, that whatever we ask the Father in His name He may give us (John 15:16) [2].

- **Persist.** Jesus told of a man who got bread at midnight only because his friend kept asking, and of a widow who wore down an unjust judge by her continual coming; praying over and over with determination is a valid expression of faith, just as praying once is [3][8].

- **Stay in fellowship.** Walking in the light means having fellowship with others who are in the light (1 John 1:7); staying in fellowship is an important key to receiving the Lord's blessings [2].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapters 1, 3 and 4 of *100% Answered Prayer* and chapter 9 of *How to Pray*.

Scriptures referenced: Psalms 91:15; Psalms 119:133; Isaiah 58:9; Luke 11:5-9; John 15:16; 2 Corinthians 5:21; James 5:16; 1 John 1:7; 1 John 3:22.

items.question: In the book Backsliding, what are the signs that someone is falling away?
items.text:
It's a loving thing to want to see the signs early, before they carry you somewhere you never meant to go. Here are the symptoms the book describes.

- **Bad company.** A Christian who keeps bad friends is likely to find his way out of church one day, because bad company ruins good morals (1 Corinthians 15:33) [1].
- **Stubbornness.** A person who will not heed counsel but always does what he wants, in spite of all advice, is a potential backslider; the backslider in heart is filled with his own ways (Proverbs 14:14) [3].
- **Praying less.** Prayer keeps us from falling, and anyone who spends less time talking to God is unknowingly moving away from Him [4].
- **Not being committed.** The "watching Christians" who visit churches but belong to none will ultimately leave; God made us like sheep who need a shepherd, and an uncommitted Christian is a potential backslider [4].
- **Coldness and murmuring.** Backsliding Christians first become aloof, bored and diplomatic in worship, and those who murmur and complain often leave their churches and eventually backslide [5][8].
- **Shallowness.** Those with no root believe for a while but fall away in the time of testing, because they have no convictions of their own (Luke 8:13) [6].
- **Foolish questioning.** Raising unlearned questions to doubt the Bible is itself a symptom, since the real problem is the backsliding tendency behind the question [5].

If you detect any of these in yourself, know that you may be on a dangerous path — and that early detection can save you [1].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapters 3, 5 and 7 of *Backsliding*.

items.question: A member has stopped coming to church and stopped praying. How do I help them come back to God?
items.text:
That is a heavy thing to carry for someone you love, and it is good that you want to go after them.

- **Pray for them, and keep praying.** Prayer is what keeps a person from falling away, and Jesus told His disciples to pray lest they fall into temptation [8]. If someone has stopped praying, they are unknowingly moving away from God, so your prayers stand in that gap [8].

- **Go and visit them.** Visiting is not optional; it is how converts and visitors are kept and established, and it is work many in the church can share [6]. Go to their home, encourage them, and pray with them for the establishment of their soul [6].

- **Keep inviting them back, and expect God to bring the increase.** Lead the congregation in inviting people to church every Sunday, and do not be depressed if most do not return, because God will supernaturally bring the increase [5][7]. There is a principle of sowing and reaping: if you sow through invitations and witnessing, you will reap one day, as Galatians 6:7 says [5][7].

- **Pray specifically that they return, and return with others.** Bishop Dag Heward-Mills prays over his members, "Lord, when they go, let them come back to church. As they come back, let them come with more people," and this kind of prayer counteracts barrenness that cannot keep the souls God gives [1][2].

- **Travail for Christ to be formed in them.** You travailed for them to be born again; now travail for Christ to be formed in them, as Galatians 4:19 says [6].

- **Help them toward commitment, not just attendance.** Anyone who does not want to be committed to a church will ultimately leave it, and an uncommitted Christian is a potential backslider [8]. God expects the believer to be like a tree planted by rivers of water, and every Christian must be planted in the house of the Lord [8].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapters 11 and 20 of *Church Planting*, chapter 6 of *Ministerial Barrenness*, chapters 7 and 10 of *The Mega Church* and chapter 7 of *Backsliding*.

Scriptures referenced: Leviticus 26:22; Deuteronomy 32:25; 2 Kings 2:19; Proverbs 7:10; Galatians 4:19; Galatians 6:7.

items.question: How do I start a new church in a town where we have no members?
items.text:
It's a good and brave thing to want to plant a church where there's no one yet. Our books speak directly to this.

- **Count the cost first.** Sit down and consider what starting a church will really involve, because it will not be easy, and not many people want to identify with a small thing [1][2]. Jesus Himself said to count the cost before building a tower (Luke 14:28) [1][2].

- **Don't be in a hurry.** No tree grows from a seed into a large tree overnight, and a hasty spirit will not succeed at starting a church [8]. Don't expect much within a year, and don't be surprised if you only have twenty people after two years [8].

items.question: How do I deal with disloyal people?
items.text:
Dealing with disloyalty is painful, and the books speak to it plainly. Here is the counsel they give.

- **Teach your people constantly.** The teaching method is a preventive process every wise leader should adopt, because it fights deception — and it is only deceived people who go the way of Absalom or Lucifer [4]. Choose preventive management over crisis management, since those who only manage crises are stressed out and never able to move their church forward [4].

- **Dismiss them outright.** When Satan rebelled, he was sacked and thrown out of his position; he was not prayed for, counselled, advised, or rehabilitated — he was cast out [1]. The biblical remedy for a scorner is to cast him out, and Proverbs 22:10 says that when you do, contention, strife and reproach cease [6][7].

- **Do not open your doors to them.** Rebellious people must not be given access to the church they rebelled against; opening your doors to the devil is not walking in love but in foolishness [1].

- **Wipe out their associates too.** Friendship with disloyal people is never neutral, and someone who merely "understands" them should not be part of your team; God cast out Lucifer and the angels associated with him [3].

- **Restrict them.** God bound the devil, put him in a bottomless pit, shut him up and sealed him; binding a "Judas" means restricting him rather than letting him operate freely [8].

- **Be fierce and resolute.** All forms of disloyalty can end a church and a ministry, so you must not deal with the enemy in a spirit of benevolence [5].

items.question: What mistakes do pastors usually make that hurt their ministry?
items.book: The Top Ten Mistakes that Pastors Make
items.text:
Here are the mistakes the books most often warn pastors about:

- **Choosing to bear little fruit.** A pastor can leave a fruitful place for an address or a green card, and end up with forty members where there could have been a thousand; God is glorified when we bear much fruit, as John 15:8 says [1]. The desire for independence, money, position or fame is not compatible with the desire for fruitfulness [1].

- **Turning into a Pharisee.** After years in ministry it becomes easy to care about the best seats and who sits where; one senior pastor was publicly told to move from the front row to the second, and another shunned an entire programme because he was placed behind men he thought junior to him [2].

- **Getting priorities wrong.** Building your own church matters more than a nice car, and pastors who neglect it can end up poor and homeless; giving priority to the rich and powerful while setting aside the young and the poor lets a church die of stiffness and tradition [4].

- **Refusing to stay small and teachable.** Saul was made head though he was little in his own eyes, and one godly mother's advice was to stay small in your own eyes and you will be fine — remain teachable, a learner, not a know-it-all [3]. Pastors who stop being childlike cannot enter what God wants to give them, as Matthew 18:3 shows [8].

- **Being slow about ministry.** Slowness is dangerous; we each have our own time, but there is also *the* time, and Princess Diana died seven days after no one expected it [7].

- **Pride that makes a person overstep.** Korah told Moses that everyone was holy and rebuked him for lifting himself up, and that overconfidence was his undoing [6].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapters 1, 3, 7, 8 and 9 of *The Top Ten Mistakes that Pastors Make*, chapter 31 of *The Art of Shepherding* and chapter 2 of *Not A Novice*.

Scriptures referenced: 1 Samuel 15:16-17; Matthew 18:3; Matthew 23:6-7; John 7:6; John 15:8.

Here is what our books suggest for choosing your reading.

- **Read a book of the Bible a few verses at a time.** Choose a book and read a few verses every day, always remembering where you ended so you can continue from that same place the next day [3][4][5].

items.question: A teenager in our youth group says he cuts himself when he is sad.
items.text:
That is a heavy thing for a young person to carry, and I'm glad he told you.

Our books speak directly to this. Self-destruction is one of the key strategies of demonic attacks — when the spirit of Satan takes hold of a person, he will often begin to cut himself with stones [2]. The madman of Gadara, fully under the influence of Satan, cut himself with stones; he systematically destroyed himself, and this is a very important manifestation of the presence of Satan [8]. The demonized man of Gadara tried to kill himself by cutting himself with stones [1].

The books also say that what makes people so sad that they give up on life and become suicidal can only be demons [3]. They point to Jonah, who was depressed and very suicidal and prayed that he would die [6], and to Elijah, who became depressed after Jezebel threatened him and withdrew from his ministry into the wilderness, away from human contact — social withdrawal being one of the most common and telling signs of depression [6]. Depression is described as a powerful spirit that can lead people to commit suicide, and equally to spiritual and ministry suicide [4].

So the counsel here is to know the source of the problem and tackle it at its root [3], and to receive deliverance in the name of Jesus [3]. May God save us from the spirit that makes us put a knife to our own throats [2].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapters 7 and 22 of *Those who are mad*, chapters 9 and 11 of *Demons and How to Deal with Them* and chapter 2 of *Those who leave you*.

Scriptures referenced: 1 Kings 19:2-4; Isaiah 61:3; Jonah 4:1-9; Mark 5:5; John 16:2; Romans 16:17.

items.question: A leader I trained for years has just left the church. How do I handle it?
items.text:
This is a deep wound, and I'm sorry you're carrying it. Let me walk through what our books say about handling a departure like this.

- **Let them go quickly.** If someone indicates they want to leave, it is best for them not to stay on but to leave immediately, because their heart has already left the church [7]. A little leaven leavens the whole lump, as 1 Corinthians 5:6 says, and one disgruntled person pollutes others [7].

- **Restrict them if they are disloyal.** Binding a "Judas" means restricting him; allowing a known disloyal person to operate freely is one of the great mistakes of leadership [2]. God Himself dealt with the devil by binding, shutting up, and sealing [2].

- **Cleanse yourself of the seeds they leave behind.** A departure pollutes your spirit with seeds of hurt, anger, hatred, and revenge, and you will need to pray long and hard to get free of them, lest you fall into bitterness and unforgiveness [4].

- **Teach your people the Word to dispel confusion.** Leavers release a spirit of confusion, but God is not the author of confusion, as 1 Corinthians 14:33 says; as you teach on loyalty and disloyalty, that confusion evaporates [4].

- **Examine your own leadership.** Sometimes your style of leadership contributes to people leaving, though sometimes people stir up strife no matter how well you lead [4]. Ask whether you have strayed from following the Lord as you did at the beginning, or failed to exert your authority [5].

- **Expect God to raise up others.** Sometimes a departure heralds the arrival of God's choice for you; it was when Saul's heart departed that David was revealed [6]. Give thanks, for God will raise up the Davids of your ministry [6].

- **Do not mock others in trouble.** Those who derided another pastor for losing people later suffered the same, more severely; as Proverbs 17:5 says, he that is glad at calamities shall not be unpunished [3].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapter 33 of *Victory Secrets*, chapters 1 and 10 of *Those who leave you* and chapter 3 of *Loyalty and Disloyalty*.

Scriptures referenced: 1 Kings 11:3-4; Psalms 141:9-10; Proverbs 3:7; Proverbs 17:5; John 13:27; 1 Corinthians 5:6; 1 Corinthians 14:33; 2 Corinthians 7:11; 1 John 2:18-19.

items.question: How do I deal with demonic attacks on my family?
items.book: Demons and How to Deal with Them
items.text:
I'm sorry your family is under this weight — that is a heavy thing to carry, and you are right to take it seriously.

**Identify what you are actually facing.** Jesus asked the madman of Gadara, "What is thy name?" (Luke 8:30), because naming the spirit is the key to dealing with it; ask God to reveal the real identity of what is harassing your family [4].

**Watch for persistence and unusual patterns.** The long continuance of unusual evils is a sign of demonic activity — Job's attacks on his family, his life and his health came one after another, and they were Satan's direct attack on him (Job 1:12) [5].

**Treat stealing, killing and destroying as the devil's work.** All attacks involving stealing, killing and destruction are caused by the devil and his agents, and spending time binding demonic powers and destroying their plans will protect you from such evil attacks [1].

**Refuse to be drawn into conflict.** Satan wants to gather you to a battle — with your spouse, your pastor, your family, your child — so do not allow yourself to be gathered; strife and quarrels are demonic in their very nature (James 3:14-15) [2].

**Tighten your family's spiritual security.** Staying with the truth and avoiding deception, practicing righteousness and avoiding sin, and emphasizing salvation all tighten the security of your spirit against demons, as Ephesians 6:14 says [7].

**Deal with fear.** Fear is an evil spirit and the commonest sign of the presence of demons; it has power to change the course of your life if you allow it [8].

items.question: How do I forgive someone who hurt me very badly?
items.text:
I'm sorry you've been hurt so badly. That kind of pain is real, and it's not a small thing to carry.

Forgiveness here is not a feeling that washes over you; it's a series of choices you make. You dismiss the thorny, painful issues, give up your claims against the person, cancel what they owe you, stop bringing the matter up, let go of resentment and anger, and cancel any punishment you had planned for them [1][3]. That is what it means to release it, so that bitterness has no door left open in your heart [1].

It helps to look honestly at the offender. Jesus, as they were killing Him, said, "Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do" (Luke 23:34) — He made allowance that they did not fully grasp what they were doing [2]. Bishop Dag Heward-Mills tells of a junior pastor who once shouted and threatened him in front of a senior associate; instead of dismissing him, he told himself, "He does not know what he is doing," and made excuses for him [2]. Analysing your offender that way — perhaps they are confused, ignorant, or sick — gives you room to forgive [2].

Look at your own past sins too, considering yourself lest you also be tempted [2]. And remember you need forgiveness as much as they do: if you forgive others their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you (Matthew 6:14) [3].

You don't have to carry the repayment as well. Give place to God's wrath, for vengeance belongs to Him (Romans 12:19-20) — your duty is to forgive, and His is to repay [6]. Pray genuinely for the one who hurt you [1][3], and let the Holy Spirit help you; healing follows forgiveness [5].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapter 18 of *Those Who Are Offended*, chapters 5 and 8 of *Forgiveness Made Easy 3rd Edition* and chapter 59 of *Model Marriage*.

Scriptures referenced: Psalms 147:3; Matthew 6:14; Luke 23:34; Romans 12:19-20; Ephesians 4:32; Hebrews 12:3.

items.question: According to Church Growth, why do some churches stop growing?
items.text:
Some churches stop growing because they fail to share the burden of ministry. When the work rests on one person, the church can grow to a point and then come to a standstill, because the burden of the ministry simply cannot be borne by one person [3].

Others stop because they lack a burning vision. A shallow or superficial vision will not make a church grow; in the absence of a burning vision for a large church, real church growth never comes [2]. Without that burning vision, a pastor will not spend the time seeking the wisdom that brings growth, will be irritated by the strategies taught, and will criticize the very thing he needs most [8].

Isolation also holds a church back. Churches that do not grow are often isolated, and silently living in isolation will not help anyone who wants his church to grow [1].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapters 1, 4 and 21 of *Church Growth*.

Scriptures referenced: Proverbs 27:17; Proverbs 29:18; Ephesians 4:15-16.

items.question: And how should I deal with them once I notice it?
items.text:
I'm glad you asked, because noticing is only half the work. The books give several ways to respond.

- **Teach and prevent.** The first method is teaching the Word of God regularly — a preventive approach that immunizes people against the very problem you're trying to avoid, rather than moving from crisis to crisis [6]. Teaching fights deception, and it is only deceived people who go the way of Absalom or Lucifer [6].

- **Cast out the scorner.** Scripture says, "Cast out the scorner, and contention shall go out; yea, strife and reproach shall cease" (Proverbs 22:10) [2][7]. The biblical treatment for a mocker is expulsion — do not hesitate to remove him from your life [2].

- **Mark and avoid.** Romans 16:17, 18 teaches that those who cause divisions must be noted and avoided [2]. Bishop Dag tells of a rebel in his church whom he could not literally brand with red paint, so he called a meeting and told the people the brother was unsafe and should be avoided — that marked him sufficiently [2].

- **Dismiss, even longstanding workers.** It is essential to dismiss disloyal or non-compliant workers completely, even after fifty years, because fellowship is a choice and no one must be forced into it [5]. items.question: What does 'The Art of Shepherding' teach about visiting members?
items.text:
Visiting your people is part of the shepherd's plain, hands-on work. The book lists it right alongside praying for the sheep, counselling them and interacting with them — David rose early and left the sheep with a keeper to go where he was sent [5].

The deeper point is *when* you visit. A good shepherd stays with the sheep in times of trouble, and must be there when the trouble is at its peak — found standing by the grave, in the hospital, at the operating theatre, by the bedside, wherever trouble has struck [6]. Bad shepherds visit the sheep to get money from them when they are rich; good shepherds are there in times of trouble [6].

Visiting is also how you notice danger. A good shepherd notices when his sheep are in distress, even in little things, while a hireling does not even see when the sheep are dying [6]. And it is the shepherd's vigilance that saves the lives of the sheep, because the enemy watches when the sheep cannot see him [8].

There is a gentler side too: if you have no time or heart to gather the people and gently carry them along, you will never have the chance to feed them — without that gentleness the sheep will not be open to receive from you [3].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapters 10, 23, 27 and 32 of *The Art of Shepherding*.

Scriptures referenced: 1 Samuel 16:23; 1 Samuel 17:20; 1 Samuel 17:34-35; 1 Samuel 17:38-40; Psalms 23:1-6; Isaiah 40:11; Jeremiah 3:15; John 10:12.

items.question: How do I become a better leader of people?
items.text:
Wanting to grow as a leader is a good desire, and the books have a great deal to say about it. Here are some of the strongest ways.

- **See leadership as working on people, not holding a title.** To lead is to work on people until they become better human beings, so that being with you changes their lives forever [1]. Jesus spent three years with his disciples, and by the end people marvelled at their boldness, recognising they had been with Jesus (Acts 4:13) [1].

- **Reproduce yourself in others so you are no longer essential.** A good leader prepares people for the day he will not be around, as Jesus did when he told his disciples, "A little while, and ye shall not see me" (John 16:16) [3]. If those you lead still depend on you for everything, you have not yet succeeded [3].

- **Study leadership deliberately.** Good things do not drop on you like ripe mangoes from a tree; you have to study and discover what there is to learn, deciding to be a good minister (1 Timothy 4:6) [4].

- **Lean on wisdom, because people are hard to lead.** By wisdom kings reign (Proverbs 8:15-16), and wisdom is the master key to controlling human behaviour and dealing with leadership's challenges [5].

- **Value every person.** Every person has a value, and God often sends valuable people into our lives in disguise; people are attracted to places where they are valued, and those who feel undervalued move away [7].

- **Be at peace with those around you.** A leader brings peace rather than confusion, following peace with all men (Hebrews 12:14), and accepts people as they are instead of fighting them [2].

- **Listen, encourage, and be real.** Let conversations centre on others rather than yourself, notice and appreciate people's efforts, and lead by going yourself where you are asking people to follow [6][8].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapters 2, 20, 23, 79, 86, 121 and 126 of *The Art of Leadership - 3rd Edition* and chapter 4 of *Wisdom Is the Principle Thing For Your Minsitry*.

items.question: What should someone who just gave their life to Christ learn first?
items.text:
What a joy — a new life in Christ is the beginning of a great change, not just joining another religion [7]. Here is what the books say to lay hold of first.

- **Understand what has happened to you.** You have had a spiritual heart transplant, and you need understanding of salvation so you can grow in grace and be established in Christ [7]. Wisdom is the principal thing; get understanding [7].

- **Be taught the elementary principles.** Anyone who comes to Christ must be taught the fundamentals of the faith, and how you are taught those elementary principles permanently shapes your spiritual make-up [2]. This is why your first teacher — the one who grounds you in the basics — is someone never to forget [2].

- **Remember your soul winner.** The person who led you to Christ is the most special person in your life, because your greatest treasure is your salvation, and it came through their toil and sacrifice [2]. As 1 Corinthians 4:15 says, they begot you through the gospel [2].

- **Ask the questions of eternity.** Questions like "What will happen to me when I die?" and "Why did Jesus have to die on a cross?" are good questions, because they set your mind working on eternity [8].

items.question: How can I spend time with God every morning without getting bored?
items.book: How You Can Have an Effective Quiet Time with God Every Day
items.text:
What a good desire — to keep meeting God each morning, and to keep it alive rather than stale. Our books speak to this.

- **Feed your spirit daily on the Word.** Your spirit grows only as it is fed, so let the Word enter through a daily Quiet Time of Bible reading and study, as 1 Peter 2:2 says, desiring the sincere milk of the word that you may grow thereby [1]. A daily dose of the Word will also increase your faith [7].

- **Keep a fixed early appointment.** Moses went up the mountain early in the morning to meet the Lord, and you are to have that kind of Quiet Time — early, alone with God [1]. Jesus Himself rose a great while before day and went to a solitary place to pray (Mark 1:35) [4].

- **Come expecting to draw near.** During your quiet time you draw near to God and He draws near to you, as James 4:8 promises [2]. This is how the most important relationship of your life develops — a natural relationship grows between any two people who spend quality time together [2].

- **Let it refresh you.** A daily quiet time drives away weariness, dejection and depression; the Word is like rain and snow that cools and refreshes, as Isaiah 55:10 pictures it [7].

- **Vary how you take the Word in.** Besides reading, listen to preaching and watch services, for faith comes by hearing the word of God (Romans 10:17) [1].

- **Pray in the Spirit.** Praying in tongues builds you up in your faith, as Jude 1:20 says, and is a way of developing your spirit [1][8].

- **Make it a habit, not a mood.** A habit is an act repeated easily without thinking or planning, and good habits are difficult to form but easy to live with [3].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapter 3 of *How to be Born again & Avoid Hell*, chapters 1, 3 and 6 of *How You Can Have an Effective Quiet Time with God Every Day*, chapter 13 of *Everything By Prayer 

Nothing Without Prayer* and chapter 9 of *Key Facts for New Believers*.

items.question: How can I encourage others who are going through hard times?
items.text:
It's a good and tender thing to want to strengthen others in their hard seasons. Here are some ways our books point to.

- **Share the comfort you have received yourself.** Paul says God comforts us in all our trouble so that we can comfort others with that same comfort, as 2 Corinthians 1:3-5 and 2 Corinthians 1:4 (AMPC) put it [1]. Your own trouble becomes a message for others in trouble [1].

- **Tell your story, and tell theirs.** A testimony is an account of what the Lord did in someone's life, and hearing it makes the simple wise, as Psalm 19:7 says [3]. Bishop Dag Heward-Mills tells how reading the story of John Wesley showed him he was not the only one facing certain struggles, and gave him wisdom to keep pressing on [3].

- **Point people to examples of those who made it.** If you want to inspire pastors, show them ministers who have finished well; that kind of example gives hope [6]. Avoid dwelling on stories of those who fared badly, because that only discourages people [6].

- **Give books and encouraging messages.** The early church had great joy when they read an encouraging message, as Acts 15:31 records [4]. Books can end depression, assure you you're on the right path, and steady your well-being [4].

- **Mourn with those who mourn.** Times of sorrow are among the most remembered times in people's lives, and if you are beside them then, they never forget it [8].

- **Remember your own hardship and reach out.** God warns us to remember how we felt, and to help others in the same situation — if you know what it is to be poor, you are the one to help the poor [5].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapter 6 of *TS2. Hope Secrets*, chapter 22 of *Wisdom Is the Principle Thing For Your Minsitry*, chapter 6 of *WOM13. The Big Secret - Your Ministry Depends on Books*, chapter 2 of *Those Who Forget* and chapters 11 and 20 of *The Art of Leadership - 3rd Edition*.

items.question: Different topic: how do I pray effectively?
items.text:
Prayer that works is not doodling or dawdling — it is prayer shaped by God's Word and offered with real passion. Here are the ways our books set out.

- **Pray strategic Bible prayers.** Let your prayers be guided by the Word of God, praying the prayers recorded in Scripture — Ephesians 1:17-19 is one of the most powerful a minister can pray, and Ephesians 3:15-19 prays to be grounded in love, which matters because without love even great sacrifice profits nothing (1 Corinthians 13:3) [1].

- **Pray fervently.** Fervent prayer is ardent, passionate, zealous and eager; if someone watched you pray, one of those words should describe it, and then you will have great results [1].

- **Pray in tongues.** Every minister should spend several hours praying in tongues; Paul boasted, "I thank God that I speak in tongues more than you all" (1 Corinthians 14:18), and praying in the Spirit lets God direct your prayer and builds you up (1 Corinthians 14:4) [1][7].

- **Talk with the Holy Spirit.** Prayer is a two-way affair — speak to Him and hear His voice, as Jesus promised the Comforter who would teach us all things (John 14:18, 26) [1].

- **Pray for a long time.** Jesus rose a great while before day and continued all night in prayer (Mark 1:35; Luke 6:12); start with one hour and graduate to three, then five and seven [1][7].

- **Pray repeatedly about God's will.** Jesus prayed the same words three times about the will of God; that was not vain repetition but meaningful, effective repetition (Matthew 6:7) [6].

- **Pray without ceasing.** You can pray on the bus, in the office, in the shower — God is happy when His children stay constantly in touch with Him (1 Thessalonians 5:17) [2].

I'm so sorry — that is a heavy thing to carry, and I'm glad he told you.

Our books have not directly addressed this. They do speak about the value of staying close to other believers, if that would help.

What they do say is that we are not made to walk alone: Judas, they suggest, likely betrayed Christ because he kept leaving the fellowship to sort out other matters, and outside fellowship we are exposed to every kind of temptation [6]. So keep him near you and near the body — the early church devoted themselves to teaching, fellowship, breaking of bread and prayer [6], and Scripture says evil communications corrupt good manners (1 Corinthians 15:33) [6]. A person who is cherished and valued draws that same thing to himself [2], so let him know plainly that he is valued and wanted here.

Please also bring in others who can help carry this with you — do not bear it by yourself. And if he is in immediate danger, get him to proper help now.

Please also speak with your shepherd or pastor today. Where a life may be at risk, contact emergency services or a medical professional now.
